subtitle: How Land, Honor and Steel Bound Warangal’s Commanders to a Rising Crown

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle hero wide of Warangal fortress looming behind a stern commander
panels.action: Malyala Gunda Senani stands in armor on a rocky rise before Warangal’s stone gateways, one hand resting on his sword, the other pointing toward scattered villages and fields below.

dialogue.text: In 13th-century Warangal, men like Malyala Gunda Senani turned land into loyalty, and loyalty into power, forging the fluid nayankara compact that let new families climb beside the Kakatiya throne.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी के वरंगल में मलयाल गुंडा सेनानी जैसे लोग ज़मीन को वफ़ादारी, वफ़ादारी को ताकत में बदलते हुए लचीली नायक्कर संधि गढ़ रहे थे, जिससे नए कुल काकतिया सिंहासन के साथ ऊपर चढ़ सके।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of Warangal and its mandalas stretching into misty countryside
panels.action: From high above, the stone fort of Warangal sits at the center of a vast landscape of tanks, temples and clustered villages linked by dusty roads.

dialogue.text: Warangal in the 1200s was no quiet hill town. Under the Kakatiyas, it pulsed with campaigns, new tanks, temples, and a web of mandalas reaching deep into Telangana and coastal Andhra.

i18n.hi: बारह सौ की वरंगल कोई सुस्त पहाड़ी कस्बा नहीं था। काकतियों के राज में यहाँ युद्ध, नए तालाब, मंदिर और मंडलों का जाल तेलंगाना से तटीय आंध्र तक धड़क रहा था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscriptions carved on stone in a village temple courtyard
panels.action: Weathered stone slabs stand upright beside a small shrine, their Telugu-Kannada script sharply carved, while villagers move respectfully around them.

dialogue.text: It is from stone, not legend, that we know this world. Inscriptions from Palampet, Bothpur, Vaddamanu quietly record how commanders, gifts and fields were bound together.

i18n.hi: कहानियों से नहीं, पत्थरों से हम यह दुनिया जानते हैं। पलामपेट, बोथपुर, वड्डमानु की शिलालेख चुपचाप बताते हैं कैसे सेनापति, दान और खेत आपस में बंधे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Malyala Gunda Senani in a crowded Warangal audience hall
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Malyala Gunda Senani stands among other officers before unseen royals, his face composed yet intent, hand on chest in respectful gesture.

dialogue.text: In these records appears Malyala Gunda Senani, a commander in royal service, described as Shudra by birth yet entrusted with men, horses and revenue-bearing villages.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं लेखों में मिलता है मलयाल गुंडा सेनानी—राजसेवा में सेनापति, जन्म से शूद्र, पर उसके हाथ में सिपाही, घोड़े और लगान वाली बस्तियाँ सौंपी गईं।

panels.shot: close-up on Gunda’s thoughtful face as he watches soldiers drill
panels.action: Gunda stands at the edge of a dusty parade ground, gaze sharp as lines of infantry and horsemen practice formations in the afternoon sun.

dialogue.text: Here was the Kakatiya puzzle: high office in a world of caste, given not only to old aristocrats, but to men whose swords and service weighed more than their lineage.

i18n.hi: यही था काकतिया का सवाल—जाति की दुनिया में ऊँचे ओहदे सिर्फ़ पुराने कुलीनों को नहीं, उन तलवारबाज़ों को भी मिले जिनकी सेवा वंश से भारी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a frontier mandala as a small Kakatiya force marches through
panels.action: A compact column of Kakatiya troops moves along a village edge, banners flapping, farmers pausing in their fields to watch the passing armed men.

dialogue.text: The Kakatiyas needed such men. Their realm was stretched over many mandalas, each with its own chiefs, temples and rivalries. Control would not come from fort walls alone.

i18n.hi: काकतियों को ऐसे ही लोग चाहिए थे। उनकी रियासत कई मंडलों में फैली थी, हर जगह अपने सरदार, मंदिर और दुश्मनी। सिर्फ़ किले की दीवारें सब पर हुक्म नहीं चला सकती थीं।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Gunda in a shrine, hands folded before a deity
panels.action: Gunda kneels in a lamplit shrine, offering flowers before a stone deity, inscription-bearing slabs visible outside through the doorway.

dialogue.text: So the crown turned to compact and trust. Commanders were given nayankara—rights over land and income in defined areas—if they offered their arms and loyalty in return.

i18n.hi: तो ताज ने संधि और भरोसे का रास्ता पकड़ा। जो सेनानी हथियार और वफ़ादारी दें, उन्हें नायक्कर—ठीक-ठिकाने इलाकों में ज़मीन और आमदनी के हक़—नज़राने में मिले।

panels.shot: medium shot of Gunda overseeing measurement of fields with a rope and staff
panels.action: On the edge of fields by a large irrigation tank, Gunda stands as local men stretch ropes to mark plots, scribes seated nearby on low stools with palm-leaf records.

dialogue.text: In Bothpur and Vaddamanu, inscriptions show Gunda’s hand in grants of villages and shares of produce, his authority reaching from barracks into the soil itself.

i18n.hi: बोथपुर और वड्डमानु की शिलालेख दिखाती हैं कि गाँवों की दान और फ़सल के हिस्सों पर गुंडा की मुहर थी—उसका हुक्म छावनी से खेत तक पहुँचता था।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Gunda speaking with local cultivators beside a tank
panels.action: Gunda, relaxed but firm, gestures toward embankment repairs as cultivators and village elders listen, water gleaming behind them.

dialogue.speaker: kakatiya_nayakas
dialogue.text: Keep the tank strong, and the harvest will keep my men strong.

i18n.hi: तालाब मज़बूत रखो, फ़सल मेरे सिपाहियों को मज़बूत रखेगी।

panels.shot: wide shot of temple construction with Gunda supervising craftsmen
panels.action: Stone masons carve pillars and sculptors chip figures at a temple site while Gunda watches, hands clasped behind his back, priests conferring nearby.

dialogue.text: Nayakas did not live by war alone. Families like the Malyala and Recherla turned their shares of revenue into stone and ritual, sponsoring shrines, tanks and temple processions.

i18n.hi: नायक सिर्फ़ जंग से नहीं जीते। मलयाल, रेचेरल जैसे कुलों ने अपने राजस्व के हिस्से पत्थर और पूजा में बदले—मंदिर, तालाब और जुलूसों की अगुवाई की।

panels.shot: close-up on an inscription phrase highlighting Shudra and titles
panels.action: The camera focuses tightly on engraved words for Gunda’s name, his Shudra designation, and honorifics marking his role as senani and recipient of grants.

dialogue.text: These stones name Gunda as Shudra, yet also as senani, receiver of royal favor. Birth was noted, but it did not seal fate. Performance opened doors.

i18n.hi: ये पत्थर गुंडा को शूद्र भी कहते हैं, और सेनानी भी—राजकृपा का हक़दार। जन्म दर्ज था, पर किस्मत बंद नहीं थी; काम ने रास्ते खोले।

panels.shot: dramatic hall shot of several chiefs taking oaths before a royal standard
panels.action: In a torchlit hall, multiple armored chiefs stand facing a raised Kakatiya banner, right hands extended in oath, while court officials observe.

dialogue.text: Later, some Kakatiya chiefs styled themselves raya-sthapan-acharya—the ones who upheld or restored the king—boasting that their compact had saved the dynasty itself.

i18n.hi: बाद में कुछ काकतिया सरदार अपने को राय-स्थापन-आचार्य कहने लगे—राजा को थामने, फिर खड़ा करने वाले—दावा कि उनकी संधि ने राजवंश बचा लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a chief conferring with Rudrama Devi in a council chamber
panels.action: A Kakatiya queen, Rudrama Devi, sits in council as a loyal commander leans forward, pointing to a palm-leaf map, other nobles watching warily.

dialogue.text: When Rudrama Devi’s rule was challenged, these nayakas did not stay silent. Inscriptions claim that some stood behind her, tying their honor to her embattled throne.

i18n.hi: जब रुद्रमादेवी की राजगद्दी को चुनौती मिली, ये नायक चुप नहीं बैठे। शिलालेख कहते हैं कुछ उसकी ढाल बने, अपना मान उसके घायल सिंहासन से जोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: tense wide shot of rival chiefs facing each other in an open courtyard
panels.action: Two groups of armed chiefs confront each other across a courtyard, hands resting on sword hilts, retainers behind them, temple towers in the background.

dialogue.text: But the compact was never simple. Land, pride and proximity to the king bred rivalries. Honor networks linked some chiefs to Warangal, others to competing patrons.

i18n.hi: पर यह संधि आसान नहीं थी। ज़मीन, मान और राजा की नज़दीकी से दुश्मनी पनपी। मान की डोर ने कुछ सरदारों को वरंगल से, कुछ को मुँहज़ोर सरदारों से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: comparative visual of different chiefs visiting local shrines and assemblies
panels.action: In split scenes, various nayakas greet village assemblies, donate at shrines, and meet Brahman scholars, each weaving his own circle of followers.

dialogue.text: Cynthia Talbot sees in this not a neat feudal ladder, but restless webs of ambition. Nayakas built support among villagers, priests and merchants, not just at court.

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टैल्बॉट इसे सुथरी जागीर की सीढ़ी नहीं, आकांक्षा के बेचैन जाल की तरह देखती हैं। नायक सिर्फ़ दरबार नहीं, गाँव, पुरोहित और बनियों में भी सहारा बनाते थे।

panels.shot: scholarly montage with Warangal fort fading into maps of South India
panels.action: Warangal’s fort walls dissolve into a parchment map of South India, lines tracing mandalas and regions under later polities like Vijayanagara.

dialogue.text: Burton Stein saw similar patterns across the south, a segmentary world of many centers. The Kakatiya nayankara was part of this larger story, not a lone invention.

i18n.hi: बर्टन स्टाइन ने पूरे दक्षिण में ऐसे ही ढाँचे देखे—कई केंद्रों वाली खंडित दुनिया। काकतिया नायक्कर भी इसी बड़ी कहानी का हिस्सा था, कोई अकेला इजाद नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Gunda aging, watching younger retainers train
panels.action: An older Gunda, hair streaked with grey, sits beneath a tree as younger warriors practice with spears and shields nearby, village rooftops behind them.

dialogue.text: Over time, nayaka offices hardened into family claims. Sons of commanders inherited rights and expectations, yet their standing still depended on fresh service and visible generosity.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ नायक पद परिवार की दावेदारी बन गए। सेनानियों के बेटे हक़ और उम्मीदें तो पाए, पर उनका मान नए काम और दिखती दान पर ही टिका रहा।

panels.shot: evocative ruin shot of Warangal’s fort with lingering human activity
panels.action: Centuries later, broken gateways and scattered carved stones of Warangal stand under a wide sky, farmers and pilgrims moving quietly among the ruins.

dialogue.text: Warangal would fall, other empires would rise with their own nayakas and amara-nayakas, but the memory of this earlier compact lived on in scattered stones and village traditions.

i18n.hi: वरंगल गिरा, और नई सल्तनतें अपने नायक और अमर-नायक लेकर उठीं, पर इस पुरानी संधि की याद बिखरे पत्थरों और गाँव की कहानियों में ज़िंदा रही।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Gunda’s statue or imagined likeness fading into present-day fields
panels.action: A sculpted or painted likeness of Malyala Gunda Senani, in armor, slowly dissolves into a modern panorama of the same region’s fields and tanks.

dialogue.text: The Kakatiya nayankara reminds us that states endure when they let talent climb, binding new men to old centers with land, honor and duty instead of birth alone.

i18n.hi: काकतिया नायक्कर याद दिलाता है कि राज तभी टिकते हैं जब हुनर को ऊपर चढ़ने दें—नई तलवारों को पुरानी राजधानियों से ज़मीन, मान और फ़र्ज़ से बाँधें, सिर्फ़ जन्म से नहीं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Land, Honor and Steel Bound Warangal’s Commanders to a Rising Crown
subtitle_i18n.hi: जमीन, मान और तलवार से वरंगल के सेनापति उभरते ताज से बंधे
